concept: DataGrid is Table made into a panel of readings you can walk with the arrow keys: the same flat printing and seams between rows, with one cell holding the focus ring at a time, so a person reads, sorts and marks rows without leaving the keyboard.
family_difference: DataGrid keeps Table's flat printing and seams but adds one roving cell focus with arrow keys, a header that stays in view, sorting by column and row selection with checkboxes.

default_to_avoid.pattern: data grid with zebra stripes, a hover highlight on every row and a Tab stop on every sort button and checkbox
default_to_avoid.why_not: Stripes and hover fills tint the plastic and make every row look pressable, and a Tab stop in each cell forces a person through dozens of stops to leave the grid.

references.source: WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices: data grid pattern, one tab stop and arrow, Home, End, Page keys between cells
packages/react/src/components/Table: the picked look A, flat printing with a Divider seam between rows

derivation.consequence: printing is flat on the material, with no shadow and no emboss
derivation.form: Cells, header and rows reuse Table's flat printing, so a selected row is told by a tick and a stronger seam and never by a fill.

derivation.consequence: every mechanism has its keyboard map
derivation.form: The grid has one Tab stop; arrows, Home, End and the Page keys walk the cells, Enter or Space on a header sorts and Space on a cell marks its row.

derivation.consequence: orange appears once per unit, on the primary control's body only
derivation.form: Focus ring, ticks, seams and sort chevrons are ink, so a grid never spends the unit's one orange.

scroller.why: The body scrolls inside a fixed number of rows, so the grid keeps its height while the data changes and nothing below it reflows.

headCell.why: The column labels stay on the first line of the window while rows scroll under them, on the unit's own ground so no row shows through.

cell.why: Every cell is at least 44px tall so it is a target a finger can hit, and it is the one thing that takes focus in the grid.

selectCell.why: The checkbox column is exactly one touch target wide, so marking rows needs no aim and the data columns do not shift.

empty.why: A grid with no rows says so in one line of secondary ink across the width, so the window never goes blank without a word.

focus-visible.why: The focused cell shows the ink ring drawn inside its edge, so the ring is never clipped by the scroll window and the position is always visible.

aria-selected=true.why: A marked row draws the tick in its checkbox and a stronger seam under it, so the choice is a shape and a line and not a colour.

@media forced-colors: active.why: In forced colours the focused cell keeps a Highlight outline and the marked row's seam draws in the text colour.
